headline: The non-obvious pattern is a shallow quote cascade paired with a substantial, often larger standalone distribution layer: non-quoting posts exceeded quote-side views in 5 of 9 launches.

findings.claim: H1 is supported: all nine launches were broadcast-shaped rather than deeply recursive, with structural virality between 2.00 and 2.55 and maximum depth 2.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: Structural virality describes the observed cascade graph; it does not establish why the graph was shallow.

findings.claim: H2 is not supported across all launches: early quoters had a higher median follower count than later quoters in icon, superblocks, gamma, wispr-flow and playerzero, but not in deel, cartesia, airwallex or poly-ai.
findings.label: inferred
findings.caveat: The comparison uses wave medians, not a matched account-level longitudinal comparison.

findings.claim: H3 is launch-dependent, not a general rule: more than half of quote-side views arrived after six hours only for airwallex and wispr-flow; the after-six-hour shares were 91.6% and 65.0%, respectively, versus 32.4% for icon, 4.6% for superblocks, 34.2% for deel, 23.8% for cartesia, 11.3% for gamma, 28.0% for poly-ai and 10.0% for playerzero.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: The requested content-type comparison cannot be determined reliably because the classifier returned parsing errors for wispr-flow and cartesia and returned only an unlabelled bucket for gamma.

findings.claim: The late reach in the inspected launches visibly changes from immediate product reaction toward founder/company narratives, but this is only a content observation, not a complete all-post classification result.
findings.label: inferred
launches: wispr-flow: late posts include Tanay Kothari founder-history and Porsche challenge narratives
cartesia: late posts include the founders' India/DPS-RKP story and company differentiation
gamma: late posts include Grant Lee interviews, company history and ARR/profitability narratives
findings.caveat: The list samples are sorted by views and are not a representative content sample; automated label shares were unavailable.

findings.claim: H4 is supported: a recurring cross-category core exists. Sixty-one accounts appeared in at least three launches, spanning 31 category combinations; eight accounts appeared in at least five launches.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: Recurrence means the account amplified multiple launches; it does not prove coordination, employment, compensation or any paid relationship.

findings.claim: The recurring network is unusually cross-category rather than confined to one product vertical. For example, kritarthmittal appeared in 7 launches across ai-ads, dev-tools, voice-ai, presentations and fintech; TheAIColony appeared in 7 across dev-tools, hr-fintech, voice-ai and presentations; and LinusEkenstam appeared in 7 across four categories.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: Category breadth is based on the launch labels in the evidence graph.

findings.claim: H5 is supported in five of nine launches: non-quoting standalone views exceeded quote-side views in icon, superblocks, deel, cartesia and wispr-flow; they were lower in gamma, airwallex, poly-ai and playerzero.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: Standalone totals include detected non-quoting posts and are subject to public-post discovery and view-counter coverage limits.

findings.claim: H6 is only partly supported: a founder LinkedIn twin was observed within roughly minutes for icon (-0.1m), cartesia (2.3m), gamma (0.8m), airwallex (2.9m) and wispr-flow (6.9m), and Deel's twin preceded the X anchor by 8.8 minutes. Superblocks, PolyAI and PlayerZero had no detected LinkedIn twin.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: No detected twin is not proof that no LinkedIn post existed; the public-data collection may have incomplete platform coverage.

findings.claim: H7 is rejected as a general all-launch pattern: the recurring core contributed little of the first hour and most of the later reach only in some launches. Icon is the clearest fit at 0.0% in 0-1h, 1.6% in 1-6h and 72.9% in 6h-7d, while Superblocks had 97.2% in the first hour and Gamma had 11.7%, 15.5% and 11.9% across the three phases.
findings.label: inferred
findings.caveat: The recurring core is defined as accounts appearing in at least three launches, so the result is sensitive to that threshold.

findings.claim: The phase hypothesis also fails on other examples: Cartesia's recurring core supplied 64.8% of first-hour views and only 28.7% of 6h-7d views; Airwallex supplied 4.3% first-hour, 60.6% in 1-6h and 3.9% late; PlayerZero supplied 76.5%, 59.2% and 39.1%.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: These phase shares are calculated over returned posts, not necessarily every live quote or every X impression.

findings.claim: The evidence cannot establish that the recurring core's late posts were predominantly founder-story content rather than product endorsements, and it cannot establish one centrally operated network.
findings.label: not_determinable
evidence: classify_posts parsing errors for wispr-flow and cartesia
findings.caveat: Account recurrence, timing and content similarity support network-like reuse as an inference, but do not identify ownership, coordination, payment or intent.

notDeterminable: Causal claims: timing shows that amplification occurred after the anchor, not that the anchor or a particular actor caused it.
Whether any amplifier was paid, incentivized or coordinated with Social Capital Inc. or a client.
Complete quote-post counts and reach: gen1 recall ranges from 17% for icon to 61% for gamma, so live anchor quote counters exceed returned graph nodes.
The requested classifier-based content mix for wispr-flow and cartesia, because the classification calls failed; gamma returned 205 posts entirely as unlabelled.
Whether missing LinkedIn twins represent true absence or incomplete public-data/platform recall.
Whether the recurring core is one operating organization rather than multiple overlapping audiences.
